text:
The evidence can't confirm that the 2025 loss was agricultural clearing, and it doesn't show a cause at all.

What the data shows:
- Hansen records 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha asset.
- JRC maps 98% of that area as forest in 2020, so this was real forest rather than non-forest land.
- The MGAP 2021 map classes 13.1 ha as native forest, 0.4 ha outside mapped forest and 0 ha planted. So it isn't plantation harvesting.

What it can't show:
- These datasets detect tree-cover loss, not what happened afterward or why. No land-use evidence (cropland, pasture) was provided.
- The loss is not corroborated under the run's rule. 2025 is the latest year of the series, so no later year exists to check whether the loss persisted. It remains a single-year detection.

To determine the cause, you would need post-2025 imagery or a land-use/crop layer. Fire, storm damage or other causes can't be ruled out either.
